verdict.summary: Issue #221 is not implementation-ready. Its ownership, boundaries, failure cases, and validation are substantially specified, but required dependency revisions and rollout authorization remain absent, and the crash-safety requirement promises exactly-once external effects without defining the necessary effect protocol.

blockingFindings.title: Required dependency contracts are not pinned to merged revisions
blockingFindings.details: For marius-patrik/Andromeda issue #221 at version 83be7ee54ccec64fa87fc8d20aba5bc836299a125b1ea0fdf45a54da71ef91ca, the observed specification contains no exact merged revision and contract path for the authoritative state/memory v2 schemas or replay surface. It also depends on canonical interfaces from open issues #258 and #275 without merged revision pins. The expected state is an immutable dependency ledger identifying each merged commit, contract path, and compatibility assumption before implementation, with acceptance blocked until #258 and #275 provide their required merged interfaces. Record those pins and revalidate the exact issue version; until then implementation and acceptance are blocked.

blockingFindings.title: Migration posture lacks authenticated owner authorization
blockingFindings.details: The issue correctly identifies atomic cutover versus a staged compatibility bridge as an owner-only decision, but the supplied complete issue version contains no authenticated owner ruling selecting either posture or defining in-flight session/event handling, the single-writer rule, manager-code removal, rollback cutoff, and behavior after the first harness-owned event. The expected state is one explicit owner authorization covering those rules and the corresponding df:ask-owner control-plane state while unresolved. No worker may choose the posture, introduce a bridge or dual writers, delete manager orchestration, or claim acceptance before that ruling is recorded.

blockingFindings.title: Crash-safety requirement lacks an implementable external-effect protocol
blockingFindings.details: The specification requires that a crash between recording intent and completing an effect neither duplicate the effect nor lose its durable outcome, but it does not constrain effects to idempotent operations or define stable effect keys, an outbox/inbox protocol, remote-result reconciliation, or fail-closed behavior when an external tool cannot prove whether an effect occurred. Event replay alone cannot guarantee exactly-once execution across that uncertainty window. Define the supported effect classes and their idempotency/reconciliation contract, and add deterministic validation for crashes before dispatch, after dispatch but before result persistence, and during reconciliation.

nonBlockingNotes: Owner decision pending: choose atomic cutover or staged compatibility bridge and authorize the exact in-flight-state, writer, manager-removal, and rollback rules.
The issue otherwise provides a clear harness-owned lane, manager/harness dependency direction, trust boundaries, durable event requirements, downstream sequencing, and focused validation coverage.
